description: Two engineers curious about hackatons and passionate about software & data engineering!
summary: Fire Activity merges 25 years of NASA FIRMS satellite fire hotspots, MODIS (2000→) and VIIRS (2012→), into one continuous series. The two sensors don't count fires the same way: VIIRS sees about 4× more hotspots, so raw counts can't be chained, and once MODIS is retired a decade of history becomes unusable. I convert every year into a single unit, "VIIRS-equivalent hotspots", using a conversion factor fitted per grid cell and month, which falls back to the country and then the world value where data is thin. Scored only on years it never saw (2012, 2020–2025), it halves the error of a single global ratio (14.2 % vs 26.6 % per country and month), and the 2012 junction is invisible (1.1 %). The result is a public web globe and fire-activity calendar for any country, any day, 2000–2025 — the tool CONAE needs to keep its fire calendars consistent as satellites change.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Pick a country and a period (2000–2025) and see a 3D globe of every fire hotspot, a year × month calendar that highlights unusual months, 25-year trends, and the countries with the most unusual activity. Every view is a shareable link. Live site: https://mediumvioletred-clam-174375.hostingersite.com

THE PROBLEM

CONAE (Argentina's space agency) builds fire-activity calendars from satellite hotspots. VIIRS (375 m) detects about 4× more hotspots than MODIS (1 km), and the gap changes with place and season. Adding raw counts creates a fake jump in 2012; dropping MODIS loses 12 years of history. And since Suomi NPP stopped delivering on 2 November 2026, the series must continue on NOAA-20.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Ingestion of all NASA FIRMS standard archives worldwide: MODIS Terra/Aqua, VIIRS Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 — 548.5 million detections.

2. A VIIRS/MODIS conversion factor per grid cell and calendar month, fitted on 2013–2019. Where data is thin, it shrinks towards the country value, then the world value.

3. Satellite outages detected from the data itself (86 found), excluded from fitting and bridged with the next best satellite.

4. Scoring only on years never used for fitting: 2012 and 2020–2025.

RESULTS

- Country × month median error: 14.2 % (vs 26.6 % with one global ratio). World × month: 4.0 % (vs 8.2 %).

- 2012 MODIS→VIIRS junction: 1.1 % error, no visible jump.

- Anomalies survive the conversion: Spearman 0.895; 77 % of truly unusual months are still flagged.

- NOAA-20 takes over cleanly: 6.4 % country × month error on 2022–2025.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

One consistent 25-year baseline makes "is this fire season unusual?" answerable for any country, and keeps the series alive as MODIS and Suomi NPP retire. No backend is needed: the data is static files, public on Hugging Face, ready for anyone to reuse.

TOOLS

Python 3.14, uv, Polars, Parquet, pytest · React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL · Hugging Face (open data) · Hostinger (site). Code: https://github.com/julien-clnn/nasa-curious-explorers

SI USE

An AI coding assistant helped write parts of the Python pipeline, the web frontend and the documentation. The method, design decisions and validation are original work; all code was reviewed and tested. No SI-generated images, video or audio.
